arxiv-2012-07264.title: Interpretation of the apparent activation energy of glass transition
arxiv-2012-07264.creator: Koun Shirai
arxiv-2012-07264.description: Abstract The temperature dependence of the viscosity of glass is a major concern in the field of glass research. Strong deviations from the Arrhenius law make the interpretation of the activation energy difficult. In the present study, a reasonable interpretation of the apparent activation energy is demonstrated along similar lines as those adopted in solid-state physics and chemistry.

arxiv-2012-08782.title: A novel Two-Factor HoneyToken Authentication Mechanism
arxiv-2012-08782.creator: Vassilis Papaspirou, Leandros Maglaras, Mohamed Amine Ferrag, Ioanna Kantzavelou, Helge Janicke, Christos Douligeris
arxiv-2012-08782.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Vassilis Papaspirou, Leandros Maglaras, Mohamed Amine Ferrag, Ioanna Kantzavelou, Helge Janicke, Christos Douligeris. The majority of systems rely on user authentication on passwords, but passwords have so many weaknesses and widespread use that easily raise significant security concerns, regardless of their encrypted form.

arxiv-2105-13372.title: Curvature-induced long ranged supercurrents in diffusive SFS Josephson Junctions, with dynamic 0 − π 0-\pi transition
arxiv-2105-13372.creator: Tancredi Salamone, Mathias B.M. Svendsen, Morten Amundsen, Sol Jacobsen
arxiv-2105-13372.description: Abstract We report that spin supercurrents can be induced in diffusive SFS Josephson junctions without any magnetic misalignment or intrinsic spin orbit coupling. Instead, the pathway to spin triplet generation is provided via geometric curvature, and results in a long ranged Josephson effect.

arxiv-2204-06130.title: Impossible Triangle: What’s Next for Pre-trained Language Models?
arxiv-2204-06130.creator: Chenguang Zhu, Michael Zeng
arxiv-2204-06130.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chenguang Zhu, Michael Zeng. Recent development of large-scale pre-trained language models (PLM) have significantly improved the capability of models in various NLP tasks, in terms of performance after task-specific fine-tuning and zero-shot / few-shot learning. However, many of such models come with a dauntingly huge size that few institutions can afford to pre-train, fine-tune or even deploy, while moderate-sized models usually lack strong generalized few-shot learning capabilities.

arxiv-2205-04555.title: Evolution of language driven by social dynamics
arxiv-2205-04555.creator: Moirangthem Shubhakanta Singh 1 and R.K. Brojen Singh 2
arxiv-2205-04555.description: Abstract The survival of endangered languages in complex language competition depends on socio-cultural status and honour endowed (by itself and by the other) among them. The restriction in the endorsement of this honour leads to language extinction of one language, and rise of the other.

arxiv-2206-07773.title: CMB lensing from Planck PR4 maps
arxiv-2206-07773.creator: Julien Carron, Mark Mirmelstein, Antony Lewis
arxiv-2206-07773.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Julien Carron, Mark Mirmelstein, Antony Lewis. We reconstruct the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) lensing potential on the latest Planck CMB PR4 (NPIPE) maps, which include slightly more data than the 2018 PR3 release, and implement quadratic estimators using more optimal filtering.

arxiv-2210-04885.title: What the DAAM: Interpreting Stable Diffusion Using Cross Attention
arxiv-2210-04885.creator: Raphael Tang, Linqing Liu, Akshat Pandey, Zhiying Jiang, Gefei Yang, Karun Kumar, Pontus Stenetorp, Jimmy Lin, Ferhan Ture
arxiv-2210-04885.description: Abstract Large-scale diffusion neural networks represent a substantial milestone in text-to-image generation, but they remain poorly understood, lacking interpretability analyses. In this paper, we perform a text–image attribution analysis on Stable Diffusion, a recently open-sourced model. To produce pixel-level attribution maps, we upscale and aggregate cross-attention word–pixel scores in the denoising subnetwork, naming our method DAAM.

arxiv-2310-04332.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of Multiway Near-Separator
arxiv-2310-04332.creator: Bart M. P. Jansen, Shivesh K. Roy
arxiv-2310-04332.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bart M. P. Jansen, Shivesh K. Roy. We study a new graph separation problem called Multiway Near-Separator . Given an undirected graph G G , integer k k , and terminal set T ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) T\subseteq V(G) , it asks whether there is a vertex set S ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) ∖ T S\subseteq V(G)\setminus T of size at most k k such that in graph G − S G-S , no pair of distinct terminals can be

arxiv-2403-13854.title: On the occurrence of a phase transition in atomic systems
arxiv-2403-13854.creator: Luca Gamberale, Daniele Garbelli
arxiv-2403-13854.description: Abstract We present a simple argument confirming the spontaneous quantum condensation of an electromagnetic field in matter in the case of a multi-level atomic system coupled to a single-mode electromagnetic field in the dipole approximation. The obtained result disproves the validity of a “no-go theorem” and fully rehabilitates theories of spontaneous quantum condensation of the electromagnetic field in matter.

arxiv-2404-06239.title: Permutation Testing for Monotone Trend
arxiv-2404-06239.creator: Joseph P. Romano, Marius A. Tirlea
arxiv-2404-06239.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the fundamental problem of testing for monotone trend in a time series. While the term “trend” is commonly used and has an intuitive meaning, it is first crucial to specify its exact meaning in a hypothesis testing context.

arxiv-2409-18769.title: Robust Periorbital Distance Prediction Enables Generalizable Classification of Oculoplastic and Craniofacial Diseases
arxiv-2409-18769.creator: George R. Nahass, Sasha Hubschman, Jeffrey C. Peterson, Ghasem Yazdanpanah, Nicholas Tomaras, Madison Cheung, Alexander Palacios, Kevin Heinze, Chad Purnell, Pete Setabutr, Ann Q. Tran, Darvin Yi
arxiv-2409-18769.description: Abstract Periorbital distances are essential for diagnosing and monitoring oculoplastic and craniofacial conditions, but manual measurements are subjective and susceptible to intergrader variability. While automated approaches have emerged, they remain limited by reliance on standardized images, small datasets, and a narrow scope of measurable features. This study has two primary objectives.

arxiv-2502-02456.title: Model Human Learners: Computational Models to Guide Instructional Design
arxiv-2502-02456.creator: Christopher J. MacLellan (cmaclell@gatech.edu)
arxiv-2502-02456.description: Abstract Instructional designers face an overwhelming array of design choices, making it challenging to identify the most effective interventions. To address this issue, I propose the concept of a Model Human Learner , a unified computational model of learning that can aid designers in evaluating candidate interventions.

arxiv-2503-00110.title: CMB Constraints on Loop-Induced Decays of Leptophilic Dark Matter
arxiv-2503-00110.creator: Gabriele Montefalcone, Gilly Elor, Kimberly K. Boddy, Nicola Bellomo
arxiv-2503-00110.description: Abstract Leptophilic sub-MeV spin-zero dark matter (DM) decays into photons via one-loop processes, a scenario that has been in part overlooked in current literature. In this work, we provide updated and comprehensive upper limits on scalar, pseudo-scalar, and axion-like DM-electron couplings based on the latest NPIPE cosmic microwave background data from Planck .

arxiv-2510-24822.title: Managing Administrative Law Cases using an Adaptable Model-driven Norm-enforcing Tool
arxiv-2510-24822.creator: Marten C. Steketee, Nina M. Verheijen, L. Thomas van Binsbergen
arxiv-2510-24822.description: Abstract Governmental organisations cope with many laws and policies when handling administrative law cases. Making sure these norms are enforced in the handling of cases is for the most part done manually. However, enforcing policies can get complicated and time consuming with ever-changing (interpretations of) laws and varying cases.

arxiv-2512-18690.title: Photospheric horizontal magnetic field decrease preceding a major solar eruption
arxiv-2512-18690.creator: Lijuan Liu, Hanzhao Yang
arxiv-2512-18690.description: Abstract Significant photospheric magnetic field changes during major solar eruptions—interpreted as coronal feedback from eruptions to the photosphere—are well-observed. However, analogous short-time scale field changes preceding eruptions are rarely reported. In this study, we present the first detailed analysis of a pre-flare decrease in the photospheric horizontal magnetic field ( B h B_{h} ) associated with an X1.

plos-pone-0000480.creator: Luisa Bernardinelli, Salvatore Bruno Murgia, Pier Paolo Bitti et al.
plos-pone-0000480.description: PLOS ONE research article. Multiple genome screens have been performed to identify regions in linkage or association with Multiple Sclerosis (MS, OMIM 126200), but little overlap has been found among them. This may be, in part, due to a low statistical power to detect small genetic effects and to genetic h

pmc-10623799.title: Spatiotemporal description of African swine fever virus nucleic acid and antibodies detected in pigs sampled at abattoirs in the greater Kampala metropolitan area, Uganda from May 2021 through June 2022
pmc-10623799.creator: Rodney Okwasiimire, Edrine B Kayaga, John E Ekakoro, Dickson Ndoboli, Kate Schumann, Bonto Faburay, Aisha Nassali, Cole Hauser, Krista Ochoa, Eddie M Wampande, Karyn A Havas
pmc-10623799.description: BackgroundAfrican swine fever virus (ASFV) infections in Africa cause hemorrhagic disease in domestic pigs and is maintained by a sylvatic cycle in warthogs. It is endemic in Uganda, leading to significant economic losses. Previous studies performed in rural areas and in Kampala had differing diagnostic results.

pmc-11475052.title: A Review of Electromagnetic Fields in Cellular Interactions and Cacao Bean Fermentation
pmc-11475052.creator: Tania María Guzmán-Armenteros, Jenny Ruales, Luis Ramos-Guerrero, Moktar Hamdi
pmc-11475052.description: The influence of magnetic fields on biological systems, including fermentation processes and cocoa bean fermentation, is an area of study that is under development. Mechanisms, such as magnetosensitivity, protein conformational changes, changes to cellular biophysical properties, ROS production, regulation of gene expression, and epigenetic modifications, have been identified to explain how magnetic fields affect microorganisms and cellular processes.

pmc-11514850.title: Effect of diabetes mellitus type 2 and sulfonylurea on colorectal cancer development: a case-control study
pmc-11514850.creator: Mohammad Rezazadeh, Shahram Agah, Amirreza Kamyabi, Abolfazl Akbari, Ramtin Ghamkhari Pisheh, Amirhossein Eshraghi, Alireza Babakhani, Alireza Ahmadi, Melika Paseban, Parnian Heidari, Ilia Shirinkam, Amirabbas Mehrdad
pmc-11514850.description: Background and aimsColorectal cancer (CRC) is a significant global health concern, with studies estimating a rise in new cases to 2.5 million by 2035. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is also a growing issue, with an estimated 642 million adults affected by 2040. However, the relationship between T2D, its medications, and CRC remains unclear.

pmc-11650644.title: Structure Elucidation of the Daptomycin Products Generated upon Heterologous Expression of the Daptomycin Resistance Gene Cluster drcAB
pmc-11650644.creator: Lukas Kirchner, Tessa Marciniak, Christine Erk, Wilma Ziebuhr, Oliver Scherf-Clavel, Ulrike Holzgrabe
pmc-11650644.description: Recently, a high-level daptomycin (DAP)-resistant Mammaliicoccus sciuri strain (TS92) was identified, which mediates a 33% decline of DAP when incubated in Mueller-Hinton (MH) medium. The genetic background of the DAP resistance in TS92 is a newly discovered two-gene operon, named drcAB, whose expression was reported to impair the structural integrity of DAP, eventually leading to its inactivation.

pmc-11716469.title: EEG biomarkers of Epileptiform Activity in Relation to Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarkers
pmc-11716469.creator: Andras Attila Horvath
pmc-11716469.description: BackgroundGrowing evidence suggests that the imbalance between excitability and inhibitory neural activity is a key aspect of cognitive decline. Subclinical epileptiform activity (SEA) has been indicated as a marker of increased cortical excitability. While SEA is considered as a benign EEG sign in the elderly population, recent studies demonstrated its role in the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

pmc-12528285.title: Correction to: Low to moderate-dose off-label use of second-generation antipsychotics seems to be safe in the light of cardiac adverse effects in child psychiatric patients

pmc-12549873.title: High-stability flexible thin-film temperature sensor using MWCNTs-toughened Peano structure
pmc-12549873.creator: Zhaojun Liu, Bian Tian, Bogang Liu, Xiang Liu, Jiaming Lei, Jiangjiang Liu, Zhongkai Zhang, Chen Wu, Qijing Lin, Zhuangde Jiang
pmc-12549873.description: Characterized by thinness, lightness and flexibility, flexible thin-film temperature sensors can be tightly fitted to different shapes of surfaces to measure their surface temperatures. However, the deformation in sensor installation and stress caused during temperature testing can lead to the deterioration in testing capability of the sensor.

pmc-13221765.title: Partnering with Latino communities for dementia research: a mixed-methods study of engagement
pmc-13221765.creator: Sara S. Masoud, Byeong Yeob Choi, Juana Escareño, Belinda Flores, Karla Daniela López Lorenzo, Carole L. White
pmc-13221765.description: BackgroundLatinos are disproportionately affected by dementia but remain underrepresented in dementia research. Engaged research approaches, characterized by co-leadership between academic and community partners, can strengthen the representativeness, responsiveness, and impact of scientific evidence. There is a need to better understand how methods of engagement may deepen partnerships with underrepresented communities.
